paraphrase: Before his awakening the bodhisatta divided his thoughts into two classes: thoughts of sensuality, ill will and cruelty lead to affliction of self and others and away from nibbāna, and he abandoned them; thoughts of renunciation, non-ill-will and non-cruelty lead to no affliction. Whatever a monk frequently thinks and ponders becomes the inclination of his mind — like a cowherd who must guard his cattle closely when the crops are ripe.
